newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power extends slide on gas, mild temps.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power extends slide on gas, mild temps.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) fell Monday, extending Friday's slide on plunging natural gas prices and an outlook for mild temperatures this week.
"There's a lot of gas available in the state, and it's mild," a Houston trader said.

Tuesday temperatures were predicted to range between 30 and 60 degrees Fahrenheit, near to five degrees above seasonal norms. Extended outlook showed weather in Texas would stay milder than normal for the rest of the week.

Swing gas in south Texas plummeted to the $3.80 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu) area from Friday's $4.20. On the New York Mercantile Exchange, January Henry Hub gas futures, which will expire Tuesday, closed down 42.3 cents at $4.150.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Tuesday delivery sank to $20.00-$22.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), down roughly $10.00 from Friday's $30.00-$35.00 for Monday.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Tuesday's heavy load hours was assessed in the $19.00-$21.00 range.
Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Tuesday were slipped to $10.00-$14.00, sharply lower than Friday's $20.00-$25.00.

ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Tuesday's light load hours was notationally pegged at $9.00-$13.00. ERCOT January/February prices were valued near $39.00, compared with Friday's $38.50-$40.00 quote for Monday.
